cards.front: Recall a key point about The Muscular System
cards.back: The human body has over 600 skeletal muscles . For GCSE PE, you must know the location and function of the major muscles listed below.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Muscular System
cards.back: Muscles work in antagonistic pairs - when one muscle contracts (shortens), the other relaxes (lengthens). This allows bones to move at joints in opposite directions.

cards.front: What should you know about agonist (prime mover)?
cards.back: The muscle that contracts to produce the desired movement. It is the main muscle responsible for the action.

cards.front: What should you know about antagonist?
cards.back: The muscle that relaxes (lengthens) to allow the agonist to work. It may offer some controlled resistance to smooth the movement.

cards.front: What should you know about fixator (stabiliser)?
cards.back: A muscle that contracts isometrically to stabilise the origin of the agonist so it can work effectively. It holds a body part steady while another part moves.

cards.front: What should you know about isotonic contraction?
cards.back: The muscle changes length while producing force. Two types exist: Concentric: The muscle shortens as it contracts (e.g. upward phase of a bicep curl) Eccentric: The muscle lengthens as it contracts under tension (e.g. controlled downward phase of a bicep curl)

cards.front: What should you know about isometric contraction?
cards.back: The muscle produces force but does not change length. The joint angle stays the same and no visible movement occurs.

cards.front: What should you know about pe exam tips — the muscular system?
cards.back: 1. For The Muscular System questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link your understanding of The Muscular System to real-world contexts where possible 5. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question
Front of upper arm (e.g. Flexes the elbow)
Back of upper arm (e.g. Extends the elbow)
Shoulder (e.g. Abducts the arm at the shoulder)
Chest (e.g. Adducts and flexes the arm at the shoulder)
Back (lateral/sides) (e.g. Adducts and extends the arm at the shoulder)
Front of trunk (e.g. Flexes the trunk; core stability)
Buttocks (e.g. Extends and abducts the leg at the hip)
